events.title: Emperor Caracalla Is Assassinated
events.description: While traveling toward a campaign against Parthia, the Roman emperor Caracalla was killed by members of his own entourage. His Praetorian Guard prefect, Macrinus, took the throne soon afterward.
events.significance: Macrinus became the first Roman emperor who was not a senator, which showed how much power the military now held over the succession.

events.title: Krak des Chevaliers Falls to Sultan Baibars
events.description: The Mamluk sultan Baibars captured Krak des Chevaliers, the great Crusader castle in Syria. It was one of the strongest fortresses of the medieval world.
events.significance: Its fall was a major step in the collapse of the Crusader states in the Levant.

events.title: The Seventeenth Amendment Is Ratified
events.description: The Seventeenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was ratified. It moved the choice of U.S. senators from state legislatures to a direct vote of the people.
events.significance: It changed how the U.S. Senate is chosen and expanded the role of voters in American government.

events.title: Pablo Picasso Dies at 91
events.description: Pablo Picasso died of heart failure at his home in Mougins, France. He was one of the most influential artists of the 20th century and co-founded Cubism.
events.significance: His work, from 'Guernica' to his many experiments in style, reshaped modern art and still influences artists today.

events.title: Hank Aaron Hits Home Run No. 715
events.description: In Atlanta, Braves slugger Hank Aaron hit his 715th career home run. That broke Babe Ruth's long-standing all-time record.
events.significance: Aaron broke the record while facing intense pressure and racist threats. The moment is remembered as a landmark of perseverance in American sports.
